words.ex: He has a deep wrinkle on his forehead.
words.ex_cn: 他的额头上有一道深深的皱纹。
words.en: A wrinkle is a small line or fold in something, especially fabric or the skin.

words.tr:
v. 建造；构造；
n. 概念；
words.ex: They construct houses with bricks.
words.ex_cn: 他们用砖块建造房屋。
words.en: To construct something means to build or create it, usually something large such as a building, road, or machine.

words.ex: The fence marks the boundary between the two gardens.
words.ex_cn: 这道围栏标志着两个花园的分界线。
words.en: A boundary is a real or imagined line that marks the edge or limit of something.

words.tr:
v. 提取；
n. 摘录；提取物；
words.ex: They extract oil from plants.
words.ex_cn: 他们从植物中提取油。
words.en: To remove or take out something, especially by effort or force.

words.tr:
n. 强烈的性欲；强烈的欲望
v. 对…有极强的性欲（或欲望）
words.ex: His lust for power ruined his relationships.
words.ex_cn: 他对权力的强烈欲望毁掉了他的关系。
words.en: Lust is a strong feeling of wanting to have or to do something, especially sexual desire.

words.ex: The baby smiled at the sweet melody.
words.ex_cn: 宝宝听到了甜美的旋律，笑了。
words.en: A melody is a sequence of single notes that is musically satisfying.

words.ex: The division of the cake was fair.
words.ex_cn: 蛋糕的划分是公平的。
words.en: The act or process of dividing something into parts or the state of being divided.

words.ex: The shopkeeper will evaluate the old watch.
words.ex_cn: 店主将估价这块旧手表。
words.en: If you evaluate something or someone, you consider them in order to make a judgment about them, for example about how good or bad they are.

words.ex: Bees help to fertilize flowers.
words.ex_cn: 蜜蜂帮助花朵受精。
words.en: To fertilize means to make soil or land more fertile or productive by adding substances to it, or to cause an egg, female animal, or plant to develop a new individual by introducing male reproductive material.

words.ex: The volcano spilled hot lava down the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 火山喷出炽热的岩浆流下山。
words.en: Lava is the molten rock that comes out of a volcano during an eruption.

words.tr:
adj. 近似的；大约的；
v. 接近；
words.ex: The approximate cost is $50.
words.ex_cn: 费用大约是50美元。
words.en: An approximate number, time, or position is close to the correct number, time, or position, but is not exact.

words.ex: He exaggerates his achievements to impress others.
words.ex_cn: 他夸张自己的成就来给别人留下印象。
words.en: If you exaggerate, you indicate that something is, for example, worse or more important than it really is.

words.ex: The company suffered a big loss last year.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司去年遭受了巨大损失。
words.en: Loss is the fact of no longer having something or having less of it than you used to have, or the process by which this happens.

words.ex: She is flexible with her schedule.
words.ex_cn: 她的日程安排很灵活。
words.en: Able to change or be changed easily according to the situation.

words.ex: Small commerce helps local towns grow.
words.ex_cn: 小商业有助于小镇的发展。
words.en: Commerce is the activity of buying and selling things, especially on a large scale.

words.tr:
n. 律师；劝告
v. 提供咨询；劝告
words.ex: He hired a counsel to defend him in court.
words.ex_cn: 他聘请了一名律师为他在法庭上辩护。
words.en: Counsel refers to the act of giving advice or guidance, especially in a legal context, or to the person who provides such advice.

words.ex: The team went on an expedition to the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 这支队伍去山上探险了。
words.en: An expedition is an organized journey that is made for a particular purpose such as exploration.

words.ex: Farmers spread lime on the soil to make it less acidic.
words.ex_cn: 农民在土壤上撒石灰以降低其酸性。
words.en: Lime is a white substance obtained by heating limestone, used in making cement and in farming to improve soil. It is also a small green fruit that is similar to a lemon.

words.tr:
v. 屠杀 
n. 大屠杀
words.ex: The soldiers committed a massacre in the village.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们在村庄里进行了大屠杀。
words.en: The indiscriminate killing of a large number of people.

words.ex: The garden has fragrant flowers.
words.ex_cn: 这个花园里有芳香的花。
words.en: Having a pleasant or sweet smell.

words.ex: The rendition of the song by the singer moved everyone.
words.ex_cn: 歌手对这首歌的演出打动了所有人。
words.en: A rendition of a play, poem, or piece of music is a performance of it.

words.ex: The teacher will authorise the trip next week.
words.ex_cn: 老师将在下周批准这次旅行。
words.en: To give official permission for something to happen, or to give someone official permission to do something.

words.tr: adj. 愤世嫉俗的；悲观的；
words.ex: He gave a cynical smile when they talked about honesty.
words.ex_cn: 当他们谈到诚实时，他露出了愤世嫉俗的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as cynical, you mean they believe that people always act selfishly.

words.ex: He cheated on the test by copying answers.
words.ex_cn: 他通过抄答案来作弊。
words.en: To cheat means to act dishonestly or unfairly in order to gain an advantage, especially in a game or examination.

words.tr:
n. 白鼬；雪貂
v. 用雪貂打猎；搜寻
words.ex: The ferret ran under the fence.
words.ex_cn: 白鼬从篱笆下跑过去了。
words.en: A ferret is a small, fierce animal which is used for hunting rabbits and rats. To ferret means to search for something persistently.

words.tr:
n. 劳动；体力劳动；劳工；
v. 辛勤工作；
words.ex: Hard labour helps people build strong skills.
words.ex_cn: 辛勤的劳动帮助人们培养强大的技能。
words.en: Labour is very hard work, especially physical work. It can also refer to the workers of a country or industry, considered as a group, or the process of childbirth.

words.ex: His fidelity to his friend never changed.
words.ex_cn: 他对朋友的忠诚从未改变。
words.en: Fidelity is loyalty to a person, organization, or set of beliefs.

words.ex: He infringes the rules by arriving late.
words.ex_cn: 他因迟到而违反了规则。
words.en: To infringe means to violate or break a law, agreement, or right.

words.ex: He hastened to finish his homework before dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他赶紧在晚饭前写完作业。
words.en: If you hasten to do something, you quickly do it or quickly go somewhere.

words.ex: The two teams decide to unite for the competition.
words.ex_cn: 这两个队伍决定在比赛中联合起来。
words.en: If a group of people or things unite or if someone unites them, they join together and act as a group.

words.tr:
n. 公司；商行；
adj. 坚固的；结实的；
words.ex: He works for a small firm in London.
words.ex_cn: 他在伦敦一家小公司工作。
words.en: If something is firm, it does not change much in shape when it is pressed but is not completely hard. A firm is an organization which sells or produces something or which provides a service which people pay for.

words.tr:
n. 螺旋形；陡升或骤降；
v. 螺旋式上升（或下降）；
adj. 螺旋形的；
words.ex: The snail moved along a spiral path.
words.ex_cn: 蜗牛沿着一个螺旋形的路径爬行。
words.en: A spiral is a shape which winds round and round, with each curve above or outside the previous one.

words.ex: He failed the test, but subsequent efforts helped him pass.
words.ex_cn: 他考试没及格，但随后的努力让他通过了。
words.en: Following in time or order; succeeding.

words.tr:
n. 瘟疫；疫病；
v. 困扰；折磨；
words.ex: The plague killed many people in medieval Europe.
words.ex_cn: 瘟疫在中世纪的欧洲杀死了许多人。
words.en: A plague is a very infectious disease that spreads quickly and kills a lot of people. It can also refer to a large number of insects or animals that cause damage or are a nuisance.

words.ex: The professor gave a lecture on history.
words.ex_cn: 教授上了一节历史课。
words.en: A lecture is a talk that someone gives in order to teach people about a particular subject, often at a university or college.

words.ex: He poured water into a wooden barrel.
words.ex_cn: 他把水倒进一个木桶里。
words.en: A barrel is a large, round container for liquids or food, typically made of wood or metal.

words.tr: v. 逐步康复；渐愈；复原
words.ex: He is convalescing at home after surgery.
words.ex_cn: 他手术后在家休养。
words.en: To convalesce means to recover health and strength gradually after sickness or weakness.

words.tr: v. 珍爱；爱惜；怀念；怀有（感情）；抱有（希望）
words.ex: I cherish the time I spend with my family.
words.ex_cn: 我珍惜与家人共度的时光。
words.en: If you cherish something, you care for it lovingly and protect it carefully.

words.ex: He worked hard to accomplish his goal.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作以实现自己的目标。
words.en: To accomplish something means to succeed in doing it, especially after a lot of effort.

words.ex: He burst into rage when he heard the news.
words.ex_cn: 当他听到这个消息时，他勃然大怒。
words.en: Rage is a feeling of intense anger that is difficult to control.

words.ex: The doctor will weigh the baby at the clinic.
words.ex_cn: 医生将在诊所称量婴儿的体重。
words.en: To weigh something means to measure how heavy it is, usually by using scales. It can also mean to consider something carefully before making a decision.

words.tr:
n. 媒介；方法；
adj. 中等的；适中的；
words.ex: TV is a popular medium for advertising.
words.ex_cn: 电视是一种流行的广告媒介。
words.en: A medium is a method or way of expressing something.

words.tr:
v. 狼吞虎咽；吞并；火鸡咯咯叫
n. 火鸡叫声
words.ex: The dog will gobble up its food quickly.
words.ex_cn: 狗会很快把食物狼吞虎咽地吃掉。
words.en: To eat something quickly and eagerly, often making a noise.

words.tr: n. 外交；外交手腕；交际手段
words.ex: He uses diplomacy to solve the conflict.
words.ex_cn: 他用外交手段解决冲突。
words.en: Diplomacy is the activity of managing relations between the governments of different countries, especially in the context of international relations, negotiations, and treaties.

words.ex: The teacher learned new pedagogy from the workshop.
words.ex_cn: 这位老师从研讨会中学到了新的教学法。
words.en: The method and practice of teaching, especially as an academic subject or theoretical concept.

words.tr:
n. 总计；集合体
adj. 合计的；总的
v. （使）聚集；聚合；总计为
words.ex: The aggregate of all sales this month is $50,000.
words.ex_cn: 本月所有销售额的总计是5万美元。
words.en: An aggregate is a number of things or people that are considered as a group or a whole.

words.ex: The critic praised the new movie.
words.ex_cn: 这位评论家称赞了这部新电影。
words.en: A critic is a person who expresses opinions about the good and bad qualities of books, films, music, etc.

words.ex: He nodded in a blink.
words.ex_cn: 他一眨眼就点了点头。
words.en: To shut and open the eyes quickly, typically involuntarily.

words.tr: adj. 仁慈的；慈善事业的；
words.ex: She gave charitable donations to the poor.
words.ex_cn: 她向穷人捐赠了仁慈的善款。
words.en: A charitable organization or activity helps and supports people who are ill, very poor, or who have disabilities.

words.ex: The probability of rain tomorrow is high.
words.ex_cn: 明天下雨的概率很高。
words.en: A probability is a measure of how likely it is that some event will occur.

words.tr:
n. 奖品；裁定；
v. 授予；
words.ex: He received an award for best student.
words.ex_cn: 他获得了最佳学生奖。
words.en: An award is a prize or other mark of recognition given in honor of an achievement.

words.ex: This town has a peculiar custom of dancing at midnight.
words.ex_cn: 这个小镇有一个独特的午夜跳舞习俗。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as peculiar, you think that they are strange or unusual, sometimes in an unpleasant way.

words.ex: His ingenuity solved the problem with a simple tool.
words.ex_cn: 他的独创力用一个简单的工具解决了问题。
words.en: Ingenuity is the ability to think of clever and original ways to solve problems.

words.tr:
n. 面试；访谈；
v. 面试；接见；
words.ex: He has an interview tomorrow for a new job.
words.ex_cn: 他明天有一场新工作的面试。
words.en: An interview is a formal meeting at which someone is asked questions in order to find out if they are suitable for a job or a course of study.

words.tr: adj. 值得注意的；显著的；著名的；
words.ex: This is a notable achievement.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个值得注意的成就。
words.en: Worthy of attention or notice; remarkable.

words.ex: The old house has a colonial style.
words.ex_cn: 这所老房子具有殖民地风格。
words.en: Colonial means relating to a system or period of colonization, or to the people who live in a colony.

words.tr:
n. 形式；表格；形状；
v. 组成；建立；
words.ex: The form of the poem is very simple.
words.ex_cn: 这首诗的形式非常简单。
words.en: A form is a particular way in which a thing exists or appears, or a document with spaces in which to write information.

words.ex: The prices fell because of deflation.
words.ex_cn: 由于通货紧缩，价格下跌了。
words.en: Deflation is a decrease in the general price level of goods and services. Deflation occurs when the inflation rate falls below 0% (a negative inflation rate).

words.ex: The sun brightens the room in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 太阳在早上使房间变亮。
words.en: To make something lighter or more colorful, or to make someone feel happier or more hopeful.

words.tr: v. 销声匿迹；突然消失；
words.ex: The magic trick made the coin vanish.
words.ex_cn: 这个魔术让硬币销声匿迹了。
words.en: If someone or something vanishes, they disappear suddenly or in a way that cannot be explained.

words.tr:
prep. 除…以外；
adv. 此外；
words.ex: Besides apples, he likes oranges.
words.ex_cn: 除了苹果，他还喜欢橙子。
words.en: In addition to; apart from.

words.ex: He propose to go to the park after lunch.
words.ex_cn: 他提议午饭后去公园。
words.en: If you propose something, you suggest it as a plan or course of action.

words.ex: The imbalance in income causes social problems.
words.ex_cn: 收入的失衡导致了社会问题。
words.en: An imbalance is a situation in which the elements or forces involved are not equal in strength or importance, leading to a lack of equilibrium.

words.ex: The monarch ruled the country for 50 years.
words.ex_cn: 这位君主统治这个国家长达50年。
words.en: A monarch is a king, queen, emperor, or empress.

words.ex: He felt ecstasy after winning the prize.
words.ex_cn: 他赢得奖品后感到无比喜悦。
words.en: Ecstasy is a feeling of very great happiness.

words.ex: He deducts tax from his salary every month.
words.ex_cn: 他每月从工资中扣除税款。
words.en: If you deduct an amount from a total, you subtract it from the total.

words.ex: His flippancy annoyed the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他的轻率惹恼了老师。
words.en: Flippancy is a lack of seriousness or respect, especially in a situation where it is not appropriate.

words.ex: She is an alumna of Harvard University.
words.ex_cn: 她是哈佛大学的校友。
words.en: An alumna is a female former student of a particular school, college, or university.

words.ex: The teacher elucidated the math problem with a simple diagram.
words.ex_cn: 老师用一个简单的图表阐明了这道数学题。
words.en: To make something clear or easy to understand by explaining or giving reasons.

words.tr: adj. 现代的；当代的；同时代的；
words.ex: This museum displays contemporary art.
words.ex_cn: 这个博物馆展示现代艺术。
words.en: Belonging to or occurring in the present; or a person or thing living or existing at the same time as another.

words.ex: The witch bewitches the prince with her song.
words.ex_cn: 女巫用她的歌声迷住了王子。
words.en: To bewitch someone means to attract them so strongly that they seem to be under a spell.

words.ex: My passport will expire next month.
words.ex_cn: 我的护照下个月到期。
words.en: If something such as a contract or a visa expires, it comes to an end or is no longer valid.

words.ex: He wrote a memorandum about the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一份关于会议的备忘录。
words.en: A memorandum is a written proposal or reminder, especially in a business context.

words.ex: His nature is kind and patient.
words.ex_cn: 他的本性是善良且有耐心的。
words.en: Nature refers to the physical world and everything in it that is not made by people, including plants, animals, mountains, oceans, stars, etc. It can also refer to the basic or inherent features, character, or qualities of something.

words.tr: adj. 诚实的；正直的；坦率的；
words.ex: He gave an honest answer to the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他向老师给出了一个诚实的回答。
words.en: If you describe someone as honest, you mean that they always tell the truth, and do not try to deceive people or break the law.

words.tr: v. 拨弄；玩弄；篡改；收买
words.ex: Don't tamper with the machine.
words.ex_cn: 不要拨弄这台机器。
words.en: If someone tampers with something, they interfere with it or make unauthorized changes to it, often in order to cause damage or make it work differently.

words.tr: adj. 赚大钱的；获利多的；
words.ex: He took a lucrative job at a tech company.
words.ex_cn: 他去了一家科技公司做一份赚大钱的工作。
words.en: A lucrative activity or job is one that you can earn a lot of money from.

words.ex: He gave a bold speech in front of the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 他在众人面前发表了大胆的演讲。
words.en: Someone who is bold is not afraid to do things which involve risk or danger.

words.ex: The president may be impeached for lying.
words.ex_cn: 总统可能因撒谎而被弹劾。
words.en: If a government official is impeached, they are formally charged with a serious crime in a special government court.

words.tr: adj. 着火的；闪耀的；激动的
words.ex: The house was ablaze at night.
words.ex_cn: 那所房子在夜里着火了。
words.en: If something is ablaze, it is burning very fiercely.

words.tr: adj. 未充分发展的；初步的；基本的；
words.ex: His knowledge of math is rudimentary.
words.ex_cn: 他对数学的了解是初步的。
words.en: Rudimentary means relating to the basic or simplest aspects of a subject, or being in the earliest stages of development.

words.ex: He flipped the pancake with a spatula.
words.ex_cn: 他用铲子快速翻转了煎饼。
words.en: To flip something means to turn it over quickly one or more times, or to make something do this.

words.tr: v. 大批出没于；成群滋扰；遍布于；寄生
words.ex: The bugs infest the old house.
words.ex_cn: 这些虫子侵袭了这栋老房子。
words.en: If creatures such as insects or rats infest a place, they are present in large numbers and usually cause damage or disease.

words.tr:
n. 猎物；受害者；受骗者；
v. 捕食；坑害；折磨；
words.ex: The lion chased its prey across the plain.
words.ex_cn: 狮子在平原上追逐它的猎物。
words.en: An animal that is hunted and killed by another for food.

words.tr:
v. 中断；暂停；
n. 停顿下来；
words.ex: The storm halted the flight.
words.ex_cn: 风暴中断了航班。
words.en: to bring or come to a stop; a temporary or permanent stop

words.ex: The painter used vivid colors to show the forest.
words.ex_cn: 画家用鲜艳的颜色来描绘森林。
words.en: If you describe memories and descriptions as vivid, you mean that they are very clear and detailed.

words.tr:
n. 脚注；次要者
v. 为…作脚注
words.ex: He added a footnote to explain the word.
words.ex_cn: 他加了一个脚注来解释这个词。
words.en: A footnote is a note at the bottom of a page in a book which provides more detailed information about something mentioned in the text above it.

words.ex: He left his books as a bequest to the library.
words.ex_cn: 他把他的书作为遗赠给了图书馆。
words.en: A bequest is money or property which you legally leave to someone when you die.

words.tr:
n. 鞭子；鞭打；睫毛
v. 鞭打；摆动；抨击
words.ex: The farmer used a lash to guide the horse.
words.ex_cn: 农夫用鞭子赶马。
words.en: To lash means to hit someone or something with a whip or something similar. It can also mean to criticize someone or something severely. As a noun, it refers to the act of hitting with a whip, the whip itself, or the hairs that grow from the edge of an eyelid.

words.ex: The recalcitrant student refused to follow the rules.
words.ex_cn: 这个顽抗的学生拒绝遵守规则。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as recalcitrant, you mean that they are unwilling to obey orders or are difficult to deal with.

words.ex: He loves photography and takes pictures every weekend.
words.ex_cn: 他热爱摄影，每个周末都拍照。
words.en: Photography is the art, application, and practice of creating durable images by recording light or other electromagnetic radiation, either electronically by means of an image sensor, or chemically by means of a light-sensitive material such as photographic film.

words.ex: The palace had opulent carpets and golden chandeliers.
words.ex_cn: 宫殿里有华丽的地毯和金色的吊灯。
words.en: Having or displaying great wealth or richness.

words.ex: The school will equip the lab with new computers.
words.ex_cn: 学校将为实验室配备新电脑。
words.en: To provide someone or something with the necessary items for a particular purpose.

words.ex: He wrote her a letter to rekindle their friendship.
words.ex_cn: 他给她写了一封信，想重新激起他们的友谊。
words.en: To rekindle something means to make it start again or become active again after it has stopped or become less active.

words.ex: He raised an objection to the new rule.
words.ex_cn: 他对新规定提出了反对。
words.en: An objection is an expression or feeling of disapproval or opposition; a reason for disagreeing.

words.ex: The two houses are adjacent to each other.
words.ex_cn: 这两栋房子彼此相邻。
words.en: If one thing is adjacent to another, it is next to it or adjoining it.

words.tr: n. 运动；动作；活动；乐章；
words.ex: The movement of the sun changes the shadow.
words.ex_cn: 太阳的运动改变了影子。
words.en: The act or process of moving or being moved; a change of position or place.

words.ex: He has insomnia and cannot sleep at night.
words.ex_cn: 他有失眠症，晚上睡不着。
words.en: If someone suffers from insomnia, they find it difficult to sleep.

words.tr:
n. 怨恨；积怨；嫌隙
v. 勉强做；不情愿地给；吝惜
words.ex: He holds a grudge against his brother.
words.ex_cn: 他对他哥哥心怀怨恨。
words.en: A grudge is a persistent feeling of ill will or resentment resulting from a past insult or injury.

words.ex: We took a detour to avoid the traffic.
words.ex_cn: 我们绕道以避开交通拥堵。
words.en: A detour is a longer, less direct way to go somewhere, used to avoid a problem or to visit something along the way.

words.ex: Loud noise aggravates his headache.
words.ex_cn: 噪音加重了他的头痛。
words.en: If someone or something aggravates a situation, they make it worse.

words.tr: v. 容纳；适应；为...提供住宿；
words.ex: The hotel can accommodate 200 guests.
words.ex_cn: 这家酒店能容纳200位客人。
words.en: If a building or space can accommodate someone or something, it has enough room for them.

words.ex: He showed strong emotion when he heard the news.
words.ex_cn: 当他听到这个消息时，表现出了强烈的情绪。
words.en: An emotion is a feeling such as happiness, love, fear, anger, or hatred, which can be caused by the situation that you are in or the people you are with.

words.tr: v. 增加；引起；筹募；提起；养育；
words.ex: The company will raise wages next month.
words.ex_cn: 公司下个月将提高工资。
words.en: To raise something means to move it to a higher position or to increase it in amount or level.

words.tr: n. 拜物教；盲目崇拜；[医] 恋物癖
words.ex: He believes in fetishism, thinking that objects have special power.
words.ex_cn: 他相信拜物教，认为物体具有特殊的力量。
words.en: Fetishism is a form of sexual behavior in which gratification is linked to an abnormal degree to a particular object, item of clothing, part of the body, etc.

words.ex: He wears a badge on his shirt.
words.ex_cn: 他衬衫上戴着一枚徽章。
words.en: A badge is a small piece of metal, plastic, or cloth which you wear in order to show people that you have a particular rank, job, or belong to a particular group.

words.ex: The bomb will explode at noon.
words.ex_cn: 炸弹将在中午爆炸。
words.en: If an object explodes, it bursts loudly and with great force, often causing damage or injury.

words.ex: The pediatrician checks the child's health every month.
words.ex_cn: 儿科医生每个月检查孩子的健康状况。
words.en: A pediatrician is a doctor who specializes in the care of children and their diseases.

words.tr:
adj. 亵渎的；不敬神的；世俗的
v. 亵渎神灵；亵圣
words.ex: He used profane words during the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他在争吵中说了脏话。
words.en: If someone uses profane language, they use language that is considered to be rude or offensive, especially because it refers to sex or other bodily functions in a way that is considered inappropriate.

words.ex: The price of oil fluctuates every day.
words.ex_cn: 油价每天都在波动。
words.en: To fluctuate means to change or vary frequently and unpredictably.

words.tr: v. 不断骚扰；打扰；侵扰；
words.ex: The neighbors harry the old man with loud music every night.
words.ex_cn: 邻居们每晚用吵闹的音乐不断骚扰那位老人。
words.en: To harry someone means to repeatedly attack them or to cause them problems.

words.ex: Good teamwork helps the group finish the project faster.
words.ex_cn: 良好的团队合作帮助小组更快地完成项目。
words.en: The combined action of a group of people, especially when effective and efficient.

words.ex: He works for a small company.
words.ex_cn: 他在一家小公司工作。
words.en: A company is a business organization that makes money by producing or selling goods or services.

words.tr:
adj. 古老的；
n. 古董；
words.ex: He bought an antique chair from the old market.
words.ex_cn: 他从旧市场买了一把古老的椅子。
words.en: Something that is antique is old and often valuable because it is rare or well made.

words.tr: n. 优势；有利条件；好处；
words.ex: His height gives him an advantage in basketball.
words.ex_cn: 他的身高在篮球中给了他优势。
words.en: An advantage is a factor or circumstance that puts you in a favorable or superior position.

words.tr: adj. 轻飘的；缥缈的；虚空的；精致的；
words.ex: The ethereal scarf floated gently in the wind.
words.ex_cn: 那条轻飘的围巾在风中轻轻飘动。
words.en: Something that is ethereal is extremely delicate and light in a way that seems not to be of this world.

words.tr:
v. 咯咯地笑
n. 咯咯笑；趣事
words.ex: The children giggle when they see the clown.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们看到小丑时咯咯笑。
words.en: To laugh in a silly, often high-pitched way, especially in a nervous or embarrassed manner.

words.tr: n. 四轮运货马车；敞篷货车；
words.ex: The farmer used a wooden wagon to carry crops.
words.ex_cn: 农夫用一辆木制四轮运货马车运送庄稼。
words.en: A wagon is a vehicle with four wheels, usually pulled by horses or oxen, used for transporting goods.

words.ex: He tried to justify his mistake by saying he was tired.
words.ex_cn: 他试图以自己累了为由来证明自己的错误是正当的。
words.en: To justify something means to show or prove that it is reasonable, necessary, or correct.

words.ex: The hill gave them a vantage to see the whole city.
words.ex_cn: 这座山给了他们一个有利的情况来看到整个城市。
words.en: A position, condition, or opportunity that is likely to provide superiority or success.

words.ex: The dove is a symbolic bird of peace.
words.ex_cn: 鸽子是和平的象征性鸟类。
words.en: If you describe an event, action, or procedure as symbolic, you mean that it represents an important change, although it has little practical effect.

words.ex: He is a dissentious person who always argues with others.
words.ex_cn: 他是个好争论的人，总是和别人争吵。
words.en: Inclined to or causing dissent; contentious.

words.ex: The police will detain the suspect for questioning.
words.ex_cn: 警察将扣留嫌疑人进行审问。
words.en: If someone is detained, they are officially held in a place, especially a prison, and are not allowed to leave.

words.ex: The lost hikers began to famish after three days without food.
words.ex_cn: 这些迷路的徒步者在三天没有食物后开始挨饿。
words.en: To cause someone to suffer severely from hunger.

words.tr:
n. 展示；陈列；
v. 展示；陈列；
words.ex: The store has a big display of new phones.
words.ex_cn: 商店里有一个新手机的展示。
words.en: To display something means to put it in a place where people can see it easily, or to show it to people.

words.tr: adj. 暂定的；不确定的；试验性的；
words.ex: We made a tentative plan to meet next week.
words.ex_cn: 我们制定了一个下周见面的暂定计划。
words.en: If you make a tentative suggestion or plan, you make it without being sure that it is right or acceptable.

words.tr: adv. 否则；在其他方面；除此之外；
words.ex: Hurry up, otherwise you'll be late.
words.ex_cn: 快点，否则你会迟到的。
words.en: in circumstances different from those present or considered; or else

words.ex: The rope has high tensile strength.
words.ex_cn: 这根绳子有很高的抗拉强度。
words.en: relating to tension; capable of being stretched or drawn out

words.ex: He has pancreatic cancer.
words.ex_cn: 他患有胰腺癌。
words.en: Relating to the pancreas, a large gland behind the stomach that secretes digestive enzymes and the hormones insulin and glucagon.

words.ex: The police confiscate illegal drugs.
words.ex_cn: 警察没收非法毒品。
words.en: If you confiscate something from someone, you take it away from them, usually as a punishment.

words.ex: He tried to hoodwink her with a fake story.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用一个虚假的故事欺骗她。
words.en: To deceive or trick someone.

words.tr:
n. 褶边；褶饰
v. 弄皱；弄乱；扰乱
words.ex: The dress has a pink ruffle at the bottom.
words.ex_cn: 这条裙子的底部有一条粉色的褶边。
words.en: To ruffle something means to disturb its smoothness or neatness, making it uneven or messy.

words.tr: adj. 史诗的；叙事诗的；宏丽的；
words.ex: The movie tells an epic story of heroes and dragons.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影讲述了一个关于英雄和龙的史诗故事。
words.en: An epic is a long book, poem, or film, whose story extends over a long period of time or tells of great events.

words.ex: The dark clouds indicate rain.
words.ex_cn: 乌云表明要下雨了。
words.en: If one thing indicates another, the first thing shows that the second is true or exists.

words.ex: He felt an obligation to help his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他感到有义务帮助他的朋友。
words.en: An obligation is something that you must do because you have promised, because of a law, etc.

words.ex: The reproduction of rabbits is very fast.
words.ex_cn: 兔子的生殖速度很快。
words.en: The process of producing offspring or new individuals of the same species, or the act of making a copy of something.

words.ex: He obsesses over small mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 他 obsesses 于微小的错误。
words.en: If something or someone obsesses you, you think or worry about them all the time and you cannot think about anything else.

words.ex: The sponge lives in the ocean and filters water for food.
words.ex_cn: 这种海绵动物生活在海洋中，通过过滤水来获取食物。
words.en: A sponge is a piece of a soft, light, porous substance originally from the skeletons of marine creatures, used for washing, cleaning, or padding. As a verb, it means to wipe, rub, or clean with a sponge or to absorb something.

words.ex: The magic show amazed the children.
words.ex_cn: 魔术表演让孩子们感到惊奇。
words.en: To amaze someone means to surprise them very much.

words.tr:
n. 发票；发货单；
v. 开发票；记清单；
words.ex: He paid the bill after receiving the invoice.
words.ex_cn: 他收到发票后付了款。
words.en: An invoice is a document that lists goods or services that have been provided and says how much money you owe for them.

words.ex: We had dinner at a buffet with many dishes to choose from.
words.ex_cn: 我们在自助餐吃了晚饭，有很多菜可以选。
words.en: A buffet is a meal consisting of several dishes from which guests serve themselves. As a verb, to buffet means to strike repeatedly and violently.

words.tr:
n. 治疗；疗法；
v. 治愈；治疗；
words.ex: The new medicine is a cure for the disease.
words.ex_cn: 这种新药是这种疾病的治疗方法。
words.en: If doctors or medical treatments cure an illness or injury, they cause it to end or disappear. If a person or animal is cured of an illness or injury, they become well again.

words.tr: adj. 热烈的；强烈的；热情的
words.ex: He is a fervent supporter of environmental protection.
words.ex_cn: 他是环境保护的热心支持者。
words.en: having or showing very strong and sincere feelings about something

words.ex: He embeds the photo in the document.
words.ex_cn: 他把照片插入到文档中。
words.en: To fix something firmly and deeply in a surrounding mass.

words.tr:
n. 草图；素描；概述
v. 草拟；速写；简述
words.ex: He made a quick sketch of the house.
words.ex_cn: 他快速画出了房子的草图。
words.en: A sketch is a simple, quickly-made drawing that does not have many details. It can also mean a short description or account of something.

words.ex: He spent inordinate time on video games.
words.ex_cn: 他花了过多的时间玩电子游戏。
words.en: If you describe something as inordinate, you are emphasizing that it is unusually or excessively large in amount or degree.

words.ex: The table is made of a composite material.
words.ex_cn: 这张桌子是由一种合成材料制成的。
words.en: A composite is something that is made up of several different parts or materials.

words.tr:
n. 刚长齐羽毛学飞的幼鸟
adj. 新形成的；无经验的
v. 羽毛长成；用羽毛盖上；装上羽毛；“fledge”的现在分词
words.ex: The fledgling bird tried to fly for the first time.
words.ex_cn: 这只幼鸟第一次尝试飞翔。
words.en: A fledgling is a young bird that has just grown its feathers and is learning to fly. It can also refer to a person or organization that is new and inexperienced.

words.tr: v. 压制；平息；消除；减轻
words.ex: The police tried to quell the riot.
words.ex_cn: 警察试图平息暴乱。
words.en: To quell something, especially a feeling, means to stop it or reduce its intensity.

words.tr: adj. 与好的品味相悖的；不合礼节的；下流的；有伤风化的
words.ex: He wore an indecent shirt to the party.
words.ex_cn: 他穿了一件不雅的衬衫去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe something as indecent, you mean that it is shocking or offensive, usually because it relates to sex or nakedness.

words.tr: adj. 不顾一切的；极度渴望的；绝望的；
words.ex: He made a desperate attempt to save the child.
words.ex_cn: 他不顾一切地试图救那个孩子。
words.en: If you are desperate, you are in such a bad situation that you are willing to try anything to change it.

words.tr: n. 神经病学家；神经科专门医师
words.ex: The neurologist checked his brain with a machine.
words.ex_cn: 神经科医生用机器检查了他的大脑。
words.en: A neurologist is a doctor who specializes in the study and treatment of disorders of the nervous system.

words.ex: The urban area has many tall buildings.
words.ex_cn: 这个城市地区有许多高楼。
words.en: relating to a city or town

words.ex: The king banish the traitor from the kingdom.
words.ex_cn: 国王将叛徒驱逐出王国。
words.en: To banish someone means to send them away from a country or place and not allow them to return.

words.ex: The fence encircles the garden.
words.ex_cn: 围栏围绕着花园。
words.en: To encircle something or someone means to surround them completely.

words.ex: He overcame his fear of speaking in public.
words.ex_cn: 他克服了当众演讲的恐惧。
words.en: If you overcome a problem or a feeling, you successfully deal with it and control it.

words.ex: The basis of math is numbers.
words.ex_cn: 数学的基础是数字。
words.en: The underlying support or foundation for an idea, argument, or process.

words.tr:
adj. 军事的；军用的；
n. 军队；武装力量；
words.ex: The military base is near the border.
words.ex_cn: 军事基地靠近边境。
words.en: relating to or characteristic of soldiers or armed forces

words.tr: adj. 有责任的；负责任的；
words.ex: He is responsible for cleaning the room.
words.ex_cn: 他负责打扫房间。
words.en: If someone or something is responsible for a particular event or situation, they are the cause of it or they can be blamed for it.

words.ex: The teacher will assign homework today.
words.ex_cn: 老师今天会布置作业。
words.en: To give someone a particular job or task; to allocate a resource or responsibility to a particular person or purpose.

words.ex: The indigenous people live in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 本土居民住在森林里。
words.en: Indigenous people or things belong to the country in which they are found, rather than coming there or being brought there from another country.

words.ex: He used a compass to find north.
words.ex_cn: 他用指南针找北方。
words.en: A compass is an instrument that you use for finding directions. It has a dial and a magnetic needle that always points to the north.

words.ex: He craves chocolate when he is stressed.
words.ex_cn: 当他感到压力时，他渴望吃巧克力。
words.en: If you crave something, or crave for it, you want to have it very much.

words.ex: The child has malnutrition from not eating enough food.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子因为吃不够饭而营养不良。
words.en: Malnutrition is a condition that results from eating a diet in which certain nutrients are lacking, in excess (too high in intake), or in the wrong proportions.

words.ex: The vase remained intact after the fall.
words.ex_cn: 花瓶从高处摔下后依然完整无缺。
words.en: Something that is intact is complete and has not been damaged or changed.

words.tr: adj. 邪恶的；险恶的；不祥的
words.ex: The old house looked sinister in the moonlight.
words.ex_cn: 那座老房子在月光下显得阴森可怖。
words.en: Something that is sinister seems evil or harmful.

words.tr:
adj. 不满的；不服的
n. 不满现状的人；反抗者
words.ex: The malcontent workers complained about low pay.
words.ex_cn: 不满的员工抱怨工资太低。
words.en: A malcontent is a person who is dissatisfied and rebellious.

words.tr:
adj. 激进的；好战的
n. 激进；好战
words.ex: He is a militant who protests every day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个每天抗议的激进分子。
words.en: A militant person is someone who is engaged in warfare or combat, or who is aggressively active in a cause.

words.ex: He did a preliminary test before the main experiment.
words.ex_cn: 他在主要实验之前做了一个初步测试。
words.en: Preliminary means something that is done or happens before the main part or event, especially as an introduction or preparation.

words.ex: The foregoing example shows the problem clearly.
words.ex_cn: 上述例子清楚地展示了这个问题。
words.en: You use foregoing to refer to something that has just been mentioned or described.

words.ex: His belief in honesty never changed.
words.ex_cn: 他对诚实的信念从未改变。
words.en: A belief is a strong feeling that something is true or exists.

words.ex: He is cocky after winning the game.
words.ex_cn: 他赢了比赛后很自负。
words.en: If you say that someone is cocky, you mean they are very confident about their abilities or achievements, in a way that you find annoying.

words.tr:
v. 力劝；
n. 强烈欲望；
words.ex: My teacher urged me to study harder.
words.ex_cn: 我的老师力劝我更加努力学习。
words.en: If you urge someone to do something, you try hard to persuade them to do it.

words.ex: The job position is still vacant.
words.ex_cn: 这个职位仍然空缺。
words.en: If something is vacant, it is not being used by anyone.

words.ex: The ball has a convex surface.
words.ex_cn: 这个球有一个凸出的表面。
words.en: A convex surface curves outward in the middle.

words.ex: He reads the unabridged version of the novel.
words.ex_cn: 他读这部小说的完整版。
words.en: An unabridged book, speech, or article is in its original form and has not been made shorter.

words.tr: adj. 不留心的；不注意的
words.ex: He was heedless of the warning signs.
words.ex_cn: 他对警告信号毫不在意。
words.en: If you are heedless of someone or something, you do not take any notice of them.

words.tr:
n. 对照；反差；对立；
v. 对比；和...形成对照；
words.ex: The contrast between light and dark is clear in the photo.
words.ex_cn: 这张照片中明暗的对照很明显。
words.en: A contrast is a great difference between two or more things which is clear when you compare them.

words.ex: Wearing shorts to the meeting is inappropriate.
words.ex_cn: 穿短裤去参加会议是不合适的。
words.en: If you say that something is inappropriate, you are criticizing it because you think it is not suitable for a particular situation or purpose.

words.ex: The error is negligible.
words.ex_cn: 这个误差可以忽略。
words.en: If you describe something as negligible, you mean that it is so small or unimportant that it is not worth considering or worrying about.

words.ex: He likes to flaunt his new car.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢炫耀他的新车。
words.en: If you flaunt something, you show it off in a way that is intended to attract people's attention and make them envious.

words.ex: The delivery of the package took three days.
words.ex_cn: 这个包裹的交付花了三天时间。
words.en: The act of delivering letters, parcels, or goods.

words.tr:
adj. 壮丽的；堂皇的；重大的；总的；
n. 大钢琴；
words.ex: The grand castle stood on the hill.
words.ex_cn: 壮丽的城堡矗立在山上。
words.en: If you describe a building or a piece of scenery as grand, you mean that its size or appearance is very impressive.

words.tr: adj. 无可挑剔的；无瑕疵的；
words.ex: Her impeccable manners impressed everyone at the dinner.
words.ex_cn: 她无可挑剔的礼仪让晚宴上的每个人都印象深刻。
words.en: If you describe something as impeccable, you are emphasizing that it is perfect and has no faults.

words.tr:
v. 撞；碰上；颠簸行进；
n. 碰撞；猛击；肿块；凸块；
words.ex: He bumped the table and spilled his drink.
words.ex_cn: 他撞到了桌子，打翻了饮料。
words.en: If you bump into something or someone, you accidentally hit them while you are moving.

words.tr:
v. （使）结冰；（使）冻结；
n. 严寒期；冻结；
words.ex: The water will freeze in cold weather.
words.ex_cn: 水在寒冷的天气里会结冰。
words.en: If a liquid or a substance containing a liquid freezes, or if something freezes it, it becomes solid because of low temperatures.

words.ex: The global climate conference was held in Paris.
words.ex_cn: 全球气候大会在巴黎举行。
words.en: A conference is a meeting of people who share the same interests or profession.

words.ex: The room was stuffy and hard to breathe in.
words.ex_cn: 房间闷热得让人难以呼吸。
words.en: If you describe a place as stuffy, you mean that it is unpleasantly warm and has no fresh air.

words.ex: The invention of the wheel was a landmark in human history.
words.ex_cn: 轮子的发明是人类历史上的一个里程碑。
words.en: A landmark is a building or feature of a landscape that is easily seen and recognized from a distance, especially one that enables someone to establish their location.

words.ex: The child hurt his limb while playing.
words.ex_cn: 孩子玩耍时伤到了肢体。
words.en: A limb is one of the jointed appendages of an animal used for locomotion or grasping: arm; leg; wing; flipper.

words.ex: The rain and the thunder happened in conjunction.
words.ex_cn: 雨和雷声同时发生。
words.en: A conjunction is a word that is used to connect clauses or sentences or to coordinate words in the same clause.

words.ex: The bird glide smoothly over the lake.
words.ex_cn: 鸟儿在湖面上滑行。
words.en: To move smoothly and continuously along, as if without effort or resistance.

words.ex: He goes to kindergarten every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上上幼儿园。
words.en: A kindergarten is a school or class for young children, usually between the ages of four and six.

words.ex: The teacher gave a descriptive answer about the painting.
words.ex_cn: 老师对这幅画给出了一个描述性的回答。
words.en: If you describe something as descriptive, you mean that it gives a detailed account of something.

words.ex: Parental love is very important for children.
words.ex_cn: 父母的爱对孩子非常重要。
words.en: Relating to or characteristic of a parent or parents.

words.ex: He shared his opinion about the movie.
words.ex_cn: 他分享了他对这部电影的意见。
words.en: Your ideas or beliefs about a particular subject.

words.tr:
adj. 有规律的；经常的；常见的；
n. 常客；
words.ex: He goes for a run every morning, a regular habit.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上跑步，这是一个有规律的习惯。
words.en: Something that is regular happens or is done at equal intervals or is consistent in pattern or occurrence.

words.ex: It was futile to try to fix the broken clock.
words.ex_cn: 试图修理坏掉的钟表是徒劳的。
words.en: If you say that something is futile, you mean there is no point in doing it, usually because it has no chance of succeeding.

words.ex: People congregate in the park on weekends.
words.ex_cn: 人们在周末聚集在公园里。
words.en: To congregate means to come together in a group or crowd.

words.ex: She bought a new outfit for the party.
words.ex_cn: 她为派对买了一套新衣服。
words.en: An outfit is a set of clothes worn together, especially for a particular occasion or purpose.

words.ex: The noise infuriates my neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 噪音让我的邻居非常生气。
words.en: To make someone extremely angry.

words.tr:
n. 液体；
adj. 液态的；
words.ex: Water is a common liquid.
words.ex_cn: 水是一种常见的液体。
words.en: A liquid is a substance which is not solid but which flows and can be poured, for example water.

words.tr: v. 重获；夺回；收复；回想
words.ex: He tried to recapture his childhood joy.
words.ex_cn: 他试图重新捕捉童年的快乐。
words.en: To recapture something means to catch it again after it has escaped or been lost, or to experience again a feeling or situation that you had in the past.

words.ex: He defeated his opponent in the chess game.
words.ex_cn: 他在国际象棋比赛中击败了对手。
words.en: An opponent is someone who is competing against you in a contest, game, or argument, or someone who is opposed to an idea or plan.

words.tr: adj. 性情乖戾的；脾气暴躁的
words.ex: He is grumpy when he wakes up early.
words.ex_cn: 他早起时会脾气不好。
words.en: If you say that someone is grumpy, you mean that they are bad-tempered and miserable.

words.tr:
n. 地中海；
adj. 地中海的；
words.ex: He sailed across the Mediterranean last summer.
words.ex_cn: 他去年夏天横渡了地中海。
words.en: relating to the Mediterranean Sea or the countries around it

words.ex: The rubber band shows great elasticity when stretched.
words.ex_cn: 橡皮筋被拉伸时表现出很大的弹性。
words.en: The ability of an object or material to resume its normal shape after being stretched or compressed.

words.tr: adj. 可感知的；易察觉的；明显的
words.ex: The tension in the room was palpable.
words.ex_cn: 房间里的紧张感是明显的。
words.en: If you describe something as palpable, you mean that it is obvious or intense and easily noticed.

words.ex: The small river flows into the main river as a tributary.
words.ex_cn: 这条小河作为支流汇入主河。
words.en: A tributary is a stream or river that flows into a larger stream or main stem (or parent) river or a lake. A tributary does not flow directly into a sea or ocean.

words.ex: The school forbids students to use phones in class.
words.ex_cn: 学校禁止学生在课堂上使用手机。
words.en: To forbid something means to order that it must not be done.

words.tr:
n. 快照；
v. 突然断裂；猛然咬；
adj. 突然的；匆忙的；
words.ex: He took a snap of the sunset.
words.ex_cn: 他拍了一张日落的快照。
words.en: If something snaps or if you snap it, it breaks suddenly, usually with a sharp cracking noise. | A snap is a photograph. | If someone snaps, or if something snaps inside them, they suddenly stop being calm and become very angry.

words.ex: They enclose the garden with a wooden fence.
words.ex_cn: 他们用木栅栏把花园围起来。
words.en: If you enclose something with a letter, you put it in the same envelope as the letter.

words.tr:
n. 喧嚷；大声要求
v. 喧嚷；大声的要求
words.ex: The crowd made a loud clamour for justice.
words.ex_cn: 人群大声呼喊要求正义。
words.en: If people are clamouring for something, they are demanding it in a noisy or angry way.

words.tr: n. 喜爱；类同；密切关系；亲和力
words.ex: She has an affinity for painting.
words.ex_cn: 她喜爱绘画。
words.en: A natural liking for or attraction to someone or something.

words.ex: The drought depletes the water supply.
words.ex_cn: 干旱耗尽了水源。
words.en: If you deplete something, you reduce the amount of it that is available or that exists.

words.tr:
adj. 零下的；负的；
n. 缺点；
prep. 减去；
words.ex: The temperature is minus ten degrees Celsius.
words.ex_cn: 气温是零下十摄氏度。
words.en: A minus is a mathematical symbol that represents subtraction or a negative quantity.

words.ex: His rude words detract from the beauty of the speech.
words.ex_cn: 他粗鲁的话贬损了演讲的优美。
words.en: If one thing detracts from another, it makes it seem less good or impressive.

words.ex: They elect a new president every four years.
words.ex_cn: 他们每四年选举一位新总统。
words.en: To choose someone for a particular job or position by voting.

words.tr: n. 无效；虚弱；无能为力；阳萎
words.ex: The new policy showed impotence in solving the problem.
words.ex_cn: 这项新政策在解决问题上显得无效。
words.en: The condition of being unable to take effective action; helplessness.

words.ex: The new movie was a blockbuster and sold out every show.
words.ex_cn: 这部新电影大受欢迎，场场爆满。
words.en: A blockbuster is a film or book that is very popular and successful, especially one that has made a lot of money.

words.tr: adj. 虚弱的；衰弱的；无力的；
words.ex: The old man gave a feeble smile.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人露出虚弱的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as feeble, you mean that they are weak.

words.ex: He had to endure the cold winter without a coat.
words.ex_cn: 他不得不在没有外套的情况下忍受寒冷的冬天。
words.en: To endure means to suffer something difficult, unpleasant, or painful, or to continue to exist for a long time.

words.tr: adj. 黄铜制的；黄铜色的；厚颜无耻的
words.ex: The brazen statue sparkled in the sun.
words.ex_cn: 这尊黄铜雕像在阳光下闪闪发光。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as brazen, you mean that they are doing something shocking or immoral in a very open way, without trying to hide it.

words.ex: He poured water into the glass.
words.ex_cn: 他把水倒进杯子里。
words.en: If you pour a liquid or other substance, you make it flow steadily out of a container by holding the container at an angle.

words.tr:
n. 下降；衰退；
v. 下降；衰退；
words.ex: There was a sharp decline in sales last month.
words.ex_cn: 上个月销售额大幅下降。
words.en: If something declines, it becomes less in quantity, importance, or strength.

words.tr:
n. 收费；负责；指控；
v. 收费；充电；
words.ex: The hotel charge is $50 per night.
words.ex_cn: 酒店的收费是每晚50美元。
words.en: If you charge someone, you ask them to pay an amount of money for something that you have sold to them or done for them.

words.ex: His utterance made everyone silent.
words.ex_cn: 他的话让所有人都沉默了。
words.en: An utterance is a word, statement, or sound that someone says.

words.ex: He gave an arrogant answer to the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他傲慢地回答了老师的问题。
words.en: Someone who is arrogant behaves in a proud, unpleasant way towards other people because they believe that they are more important than others.

words.ex: He has a chronic cough that lasts for months.
words.ex_cn: 他有一个持续数月的慢性咳嗽。
words.en: A chronic illness or condition lasts for a long time and cannot be cured, but it can usually be controlled.

words.ex: The country is developing its economy.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家正在发展它的经济。
words.en: To develop means to grow or cause to grow and become more mature, advanced, or elaborate.

words.ex: The electric lamp lights up the room.
words.ex_cn: 电灯照亮了房间。
words.en: Something that is electric works by means of electricity, is powered by electricity, or produces electricity.

words.tr:
v. 估算；估价；
n. 估价；估算；
words.ex: Can you estimate how long it will take?
words.ex_cn: 你能估算一下需要多长时间吗？
words.en: If you estimate a quantity or value, you make an approximate judgment or calculation of it.

words.tr: adj. 徒劳的；空虚的；自负的；爱慕虚荣的
words.ex: It's vain to try to fix what can't be fixed.
words.ex_cn: 试图修复无法修复的东西是徒劳的。
words.en: If you describe someone as vain, you are critical of their extreme pride in their own beauty, intelligence, or other good qualities.

words.ex: He exerted pressure on his team to win.
words.ex_cn: 他给他的团队施加了压力以赢得比赛。
words.en: To exert means to use power, influence, or effort to make something happen.

words.ex: He went to school despite the rain.
words.ex_cn: 尽管下雨，他还是去上学了。
words.en: Without being affected by; in spite of.

words.ex: He knows good etiquette at dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他知道晚餐时的礼貌规矩。
words.en: Etiquette refers to the customary code of polite behavior in society or among members of a particular profession or group.

words.ex: The team went on an expedition to the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 这支队伍去山上探险了。
words.en: An expedition is an organized journey that is made for a particular purpose such as exploration.

words.tr:
v. 诋毁；诽谤；中伤
n. 诋毁；诽谤；中伤
words.ex: He spread slander about his neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他散布了关于他邻居的诽谤。
words.en: Slander is the action or crime of making a false spoken statement damaging to a person's reputation.

words.tr: adj. 过时的；废弃的；淘汰的；
words.ex: This phone is obsolete because it doesn't work with new apps.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机已经过时了，因为它不能使用新应用。
words.en: Something that is obsolete is no longer needed because something better has been invented.

words.tr:
n. 赛跑；竞争；种族；
v. 比赛；快速移动；
words.ex: He won the race by running fast.
words.ex_cn: 他通过快速奔跑赢得了赛跑。
words.en: A race is a competition to see who is the fastest, for example in running, swimming, or driving.

words.ex: I can detect a change in her mood.
words.ex_cn: 我能察觉到她情绪的变化。
words.en: To detect something means to find it or discover it, often using special equipment or methods.

words.ex: He is confined to his room because he is sick.
words.ex_cn: 他因为生病被限制在房间里。
words.en: If you confine something or someone, you limit them to a particular place or situation.

words.ex: The teacher gave extra praise to satisfy the students.
words.ex_cn: 老师给予额外的表扬来使学生满意。
words.en: If someone or something satisfies you, they give you enough of what you want or need to make you pleased or contented.

words.ex: He walked onwards without stopping.
words.ex_cn: 他不停地向前走。
words.en: If something happens from a particular time onwards or onward, it begins to happen at that time and continues to happen afterward.

words.tr:
v. 潜伏；隐藏
n. 潜伏；埋伏
words.ex: A cat lurks behind the bush.
words.ex_cn: 一只猫躲在灌木丛后。
words.en: To lurk means to wait or move in a secretive way so that you cannot be seen, especially because you are about to attack someone or do something wrong.

words.tr: adj. 大胆的；勇敢的； v. “dare”的现在分词；
words.ex: He made a daring jump off the bridge.
words.ex_cn: 他大胆地从桥上跳了下去。
words.en: If you describe a person or their behaviour as daring, you mean that they are willing to do things which might be dangerous or which might shock or anger other people.

words.ex: He spent the evening in introspection.
words.ex_cn: 他整个晚上都在反省。
words.en: The examination of one's own thoughts, feelings, and sensations; self-examination.

words.tr: n. 洗涤剂；洗衣粉；去垢剂；
words.ex: She uses detergent to wash the clothes.
words.ex_cn: 她用洗涤剂洗衣服。
words.en: A detergent is a substance that is used for cleaning things, especially clothes and dishes.

words.tr: v. 膨胀；使充气；夸口；吹嘘
words.ex: He tries to inflate the balloon with his mouth.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用嘴把气球吹大。
words.en: To inflate something means to cause it to increase in size by filling it with air or gas. It can also refer to increasing the amount of money in circulation, leading to a decrease in its value.

words.ex: He wants to apply for a job at the bank.
words.ex_cn: 他想申请银行的工作。
words.en: To make a formal request, usually in writing, for something such as a job, a place at a university, or permission to do something.

words.tr:
v. 挖洞；钻进；翻寻
n. 地洞
words.ex: The rabbit burrows under the tree.
words.ex_cn: 兔子在树下打洞。
words.en: A burrow is a hole or tunnel dug by a small animal, such as a rabbit or a mole, as a dwelling. As a verb, to burrow means to dig a hole or tunnel for habitation or refuge.

words.tr:
n. 要点；点；观点；分数；
v. 指出；指向；
words.ex: The main point of his speech was to save energy.
words.ex_cn: 他演讲的主要要点是节约能源。
words.en: A point is a particular place or position, or a detail or aspect of something. It can also refer to the sharp end of something, or a unit of scoring in games. As a verb, it means to direct someone's attention towards something by extending a finger or other object.

words.ex: The diamond has many smooth facets.
words.ex_cn: 这颗钻石有许多光滑的小平面。
words.en: A particular aspect or feature of something.

words.ex: The valiant soldier fought bravely to protect his team.
words.ex_cn: 这位勇敢的士兵英勇战斗以保护他的队友。
words.en: Someone who is valiant is very brave and determined, especially in a difficult situation.

words.ex: The smell repels insects.
words.ex_cn: 这种气味能击退昆虫。
words.en: If something repels you, it is so unpleasant or offensive that you want to avoid it or push it away.

words.tr:
v. 评论；表达意见；
n. 评论；意见；
words.ex: He commented on the movie last night.
words.ex_cn: 他昨晚对这部电影发表了评论。
words.en: A comment is something that you say which expresses your opinion of something or which gives an explanation of it.

words.tr: adj. 随意的；非正式的；偶然的；
words.ex: He wore casual clothes to the party.
words.ex_cn: 他穿了随意的衣服去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe someone's attitude or behavior as casual, you mean they are not very concerned about what they are doing or what is happening around them, or they are not taking it seriously.

words.tr:
n. 首都；财富；大写字母；
adj. 大写的；
words.ex: Beijing is the capital of China.
words.ex_cn: 北京是中国的首都。
words.en: The city or town that functions as the seat of government and administrative center of a country or region.

words.ex: The volcano erupts suddenly.
words.ex_cn: 火山突然喷发。
words.en: If a volcano erupts, it throws out smoke, fire, and melted rocks.

words.ex: It is apparent that he is tired.
words.ex_cn: 很明显他很累。
words.en: If something is apparent, it seems to be true, although you cannot be certain that it is.

words.ex: He made a painstaking effort to fix the small details.
words.ex_cn: 他细心地努力修正每一个小细节。
words.en: If you describe someone's work as painstaking, you mean that they do it very carefully and thoroughly, often taking a long time.

words.tr: adj. 典型的；有代表性的；
words.ex: This is a typical example of a sunny day.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个晴天的典型例子。
words.en: You use typical to describe someone or something that shows the most usual characteristics of a particular type of person or thing, and is therefore a good example of that type.

words.ex: The cosmic rays come from outer space.
words.ex_cn: 宇宙射线来自外太空。
words.en: Relating to the universe or cosmos, especially as distinct from the earth.

words.ex: He felt enmity toward his neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他对他邻居怀有敌意。
words.en: Enmity is a feeling of hostility or ill will towards someone or something.

words.ex: The bright flowers attract bees.
words.ex_cn: 鲜艳的花朵吸引蜜蜂。
words.en: If something or someone attracts you, they have particular qualities which cause you to like or admire them.

words.ex: The cat creeps slowly toward the bird.
words.ex_cn: 猫蹑手蹑脚地向鸟靠近。
words.en: To move slowly and quietly, especially in a way that does not attract attention.

words.ex: The phone has a simple interface.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机有一个简单的界面。
words.en: An interface is a point where two systems, subjects, organizations, etc. meet and interact.

words.ex: He was faithless to his wife.
words.ex_cn: 他对妻子不忠。
words.en: If you describe someone as faithless, you mean that they are not loyal or that they do not keep their promises.

words.ex: He can identify the bird by its song.
words.ex_cn: 他能通过鸟的叫声识别它。
words.en: If you can identify someone or something, you are able to recognize them or distinguish them from others.

words.tr: adj. 东方的（尤指中国和日本）
words.ex: He bought an oriental rug at the market.
words.ex_cn: 他在市场上买了一张东方地毯。
words.en: Oriental is used to describe things that come from or are associated with eastern Asia, especially China and Japan.

words.ex: The old bridge will disintegrate if no one fixes it.
words.ex_cn: 如果没人修理，这座旧桥会瓦解。
words.en: If something disintegrates, it breaks into many small pieces or parts and is destroyed.

words.ex: Farmers cultivate rice in the fields.
words.ex_cn: 农民在田里种植水稻。
words.en: To cultivate land means to prepare it and grow crops on it. To cultivate a particular quality, skill, or attitude means to try hard to develop it and make it stronger.

words.ex: The project was a monumental task.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目是一项巨大的任务。
words.en: If you describe something as monumental, you are emphasizing that it is very large and impressive, or that it is of great importance or significance.

words.tr: n. 回路；环行；电路；巡回；
words.ex: The battery connects to the circuit to make the light work.
words.ex_cn: 电池连接到回路，使灯亮起来。
words.en: A circuit is a roughly circular line, route, or movement that starts and finishes at the same place. It can also refer to the complete path that an electric current travels along.

words.tr:
v. 嘲讽；嘲弄；相匹配
n. 嘲弄；挖苦
words.ex: He could not help but laugh at the gibe from his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他忍不住笑了，因为朋友的嘲笑。
words.en: If you gibe at someone, you tease them or make fun of them in an unkind way.

words.ex: The adaptation of animals to cold weather is amazing.
words.ex_cn: 动物对寒冷天气的适应令人惊叹。
words.en: An adaptation is a film, television drama, or stage play that is based on a written work.

words.ex: The library keeps old newspapers in an archive.
words.ex_cn: 图书馆把旧报纸保存在档案馆里。
words.en: A collection of historical documents or records providing information about a place, institution, or group of people.

words.tr:
adv. 彻底地；立刻地；
adj. 完全的；彻底的；
words.ex: He refused the offer outright.
words.ex_cn: 他彻底拒绝了这个提议。
words.en: If something is done outright, it is done completely and without any hesitation or attempt to hide it.

words.tr: adj. 不纯的；不纯洁的；肮脏的；渎神的
words.ex: The water is impure and not safe to drink.
words.ex_cn: 这水不纯净，不能喝。
words.en: Something that is impure is not clean or is mixed with another substance, and is therefore often not suitable for use.

words.ex: The noise was intolerable.
words.ex_cn: 这噪音无法忍受。
words.en: If you describe something as intolerable, you mean that it is so bad or extreme that no one can bear it or tolerate it.

words.tr: adj. 不腐败的；廉洁的；不能收买的
words.ex: He is an incorruptible judge who always tells the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位不可收买的法官，总是说真话。
words.en: If you describe someone as incorruptible, you approve of them because they cannot be persuaded or bribed to do things that they should not do.

words.tr: adj. 下意识的；潜意识的；
words.ex: The ad used subliminal messages to influence buyers.
words.ex_cn: 这则广告使用了下意识的信息来影响买家。
words.en: Subliminal refers to something that is below the threshold of sensation or consciousness; it is perceived by or affecting someone's mind without their being aware of it.

words.ex: I concur with your opinion.
words.ex_cn: 我同意你的观点。
words.en: If one person concurs with another person, the first person agrees with the second person.

words.ex: The loud noise gave her a sudden fright.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音让她吓了一跳。
words.en: A sudden intense feeling of fear.

words.tr: adj. 不容亵渎的；不可侵犯的
words.ex: Her privacy is inviolable.
words.ex_cn: 她的隐私是不可侵犯的。
words.en: If a law or principle is inviolable, it must not be broken or treated without respect.

words.ex: The bacteria multiply quickly.
words.ex_cn: 细菌迅速增加。
words.en: If you multiply one number by another, you add the first number to itself as many times as is indicated by the second number. For example, 2 multiplied by 3 is equal to 6.

words.tr:
v. （使）获得；
adj. 安全的；稳定的；
words.ex: He worked hard to secure a job.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作以获得一份工作。
words.en: If you secure something that you want or need, you obtain it, often after a lot of effort.

words.ex: He finally conceded defeat after the match.
words.ex_cn: 比赛结束后，他终于承认失败了。
words.en: If you concede something, you admit, often unwillingly, that it is true or correct.

words.ex: The manager will empower the team to make decisions.
words.ex_cn: 经理将授权团队做决定。
words.en: To give someone the authority or power to do something.

words.ex: The police intercepted the stolen car.
words.ex_cn: 警察拦截了那辆被盗的汽车。
words.en: If you intercept someone or something that is going from one place to another, you stop them before they get there.

words.ex: This temperature is the optimum for growing plants.
words.ex_cn: 这个温度是最适宜植物生长的。
words.en: The optimum is the best or most favorable condition, degree, amount, etc., for achieving a particular result.

words.ex: They will negotiate the price with the seller.
words.ex_cn: 他们会与卖家协商价格。
words.en: If people negotiate with each other or negotiate an agreement, they talk about a problem or a situation such as a business arrangement in order to solve the problem or complete the arrangement.

words.ex: It's a myth that eating late at night causes weight gain.
words.ex_cn: 晚上吃东西会导致发胖，这是一种错误观念。
words.en: A myth is a traditional story, especially one concerning the early history of a people or explaining some natural or social phenomenon, and typically involving supernatural beings or events.

words.ex: His sadness manifested in his quiet eyes.
words.ex_cn: 他的悲伤表现在他安静的眼神中。
words.en: To manifest something means to show it clearly and visibly.

words.tr: v. 诽谤；中伤；损毁名誉
words.ex: He tried to defame his rival with false stories.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用虚假的故事诋毁他的竞争对手。
words.en: To defame someone means to damage their reputation by saying or writing bad things about them that are not true.

words.ex: Heat rises through convection in the room.
words.ex_cn: 热量通过空气对流在房间中上升。
words.en: Convection is the process by which heat is transferred by the movement of a fluid, such as air or water, due to the difference in density caused by temperature differences.

words.ex: The king will bestow a medal on the hero.
words.ex_cn: 国王将把奖章授予这位英雄。
words.en: To bestow something on someone means to give or present it to them.

words.ex: Birds fly south by instinct.
words.ex_cn: 鸟类凭本能飞向南方。
words.en: An instinct is the natural tendency that a person or animal has to behave or react in a particular way.

words.ex: The parliament passed a new law about education.
words.ex_cn: 国会通过了一项关于教育的新法律。
words.en: A parliament is a legislative body of government, typically composed of elected representatives, that is responsible for making laws and representing the interests of the people.

words.ex: Drugs can relieve pain.
words.ex_cn: 药物可以减轻疼痛。
words.en: To relieve someone or something means to make a problem, pain, or unpleasant feeling less severe or to take it away completely.

words.tr:
v. 把…联系在一起；
adj. 副的；
n. 同事；伙伴；
words.ex: He associates happiness with family time.
words.ex_cn: 他把幸福与家庭时光联系在一起。
words.en: If you associate someone or something with a particular quality or idea, or if they are associated with it, you connect them in your mind with that quality or idea.

words.tr:
n. 碰撞；坠毁；崩溃；
v. 碰撞；坠毁；崩溃；
words.ex: The car crash happened at the intersection.
words.ex_cn: 汽车碰撞发生在十字路口。
words.en: If a vehicle crashes or if the driver crashes it, it hits something and is damaged or destroyed.

words.tr:
n. 指挥；命令；
v. 掌握；
words.ex: The general has command of the army.
words.ex_cn: 将军指挥着军队。
words.en: If someone in authority commands you to do something, they tell you that you must do it.

words.ex: This festival is a regional tradition.
words.ex_cn: 这个节日是一个地区的传统。
words.en: Relating to or characteristic of a region.

words.ex: His contemptible lie made everyone angry.
words.ex_cn: 他可鄙的谎言让所有人都生气了。
words.en: If you feel that someone or something is contemptible, you feel strong dislike and lack of respect for them.

words.ex: The lion showed ferocity when it hunted.
words.ex_cn: 狮子在捕猎时表现出凶猛。
words.en: Ferocity refers to the state or quality of being ferocious, which means savagely fierce, cruel, or violent.

words.ex: He endow a library with books.
words.ex_cn: 他捐赠了一图书馆的书。
words.en: If someone is endowed with a particular quality or ability, they naturally have it.

words.tr:
n. 两倍；
v. 加倍；是…的两倍；把…对折；
words.ex: He earned a double of his salary last month.
words.ex_cn: 他上个月赚了两倍的薪水。
words.en: If something is double, it is twice as much or twice as many. If you double something, you make it twice as much or twice as many.

words.tr:
n. 特征；报刊特写；
v. 以…为特色；是…的重要组成；
words.ex: The main feature of this phone is its long battery life.
words.ex_cn: 这款手机的主要特征是续航时间长。
words.en: A feature of something is an interesting or important part or characteristic of it.

words.ex: He has diabetes and must check his blood every day.
words.ex_cn: 他患有糖尿病，必须每天检查血糖。
words.en: A medical condition in which the body cannot produce enough insulin or cannot use insulin properly, leading to high levels of sugar in the blood.

words.ex: The car drove slowly through the fog.
words.ex_cn: 汽车缓缓驶过浓雾。
words.en: Fog is a thick cloud of tiny water droplets suspended in the atmosphere at or near the earth's surface which obscures or restricts visibility (to a greater extent than mist; strictly, reducing visibility to below 1 km).

words.ex: He has a positive attitude toward life.
words.ex_cn: 他对生活持积极的态度。
words.en: If you are positive about things, you are hopeful and confident, and think of the good aspects of a situation rather than the bad ones.

words.ex: I caught a glimpse of the cat before it ran away.
words.ex_cn: 我在它跑掉之前瞥了一眼那只猫。
words.en: A glimpse is a brief, quick look at something or someone.

words.ex: He gave a contemptuous smile when she spoke.
words.ex_cn: 当她说话时，他露出轻蔑的微笑。
words.en: If you are contemptuous of someone or something, you do not like or respect them at all.

words.ex: The clay is malleable and easy to shape.
words.ex_cn: 这种黏土是可塑的，容易塑形。
words.en: If you say that someone is malleable, you mean that they are easily influenced or controlled by other people.

words.ex: He acquired a new skill last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年获得了一项新技能。
words.en: If you acquire something, you buy or obtain it for yourself, or someone gives it to you.

words.tr: adj. 永久的；永恒的；经久不变的
words.ex: The love between them is everlasting.
words.ex_cn: 他们之间的爱是永恒的。
words.en: Something that is everlasting lasts forever or for a very long time.

words.ex: The water supply is adequate for the village.
words.ex_cn: 供水对这个村庄来说是足够的。
words.en: If something is adequate, there is enough of it or it is good enough to be used or accepted.

words.ex: Please excuse me for being late.
words.ex_cn: 请原谅我迟到了。
words.en: To excuse someone means to forgive them for something they have done wrong or to allow them not to do something that they should do.

words.ex: The sun vaporizes water from the lake.
words.ex_cn: 太阳把湖里的水蒸发了。
words.en: To convert or be converted into vapor.

words.ex: He was conscious after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故后他醒了过来。
words.en: If you are conscious of something, you notice it or are aware of it.

words.ex: It is inconceivable that he forgot his own birthday.
words.ex_cn: 他忘了自己生日，这简直难以想象。
words.en: If something is inconceivable, it is impossible to imagine or believe because it is so unlikely.

words.ex: The outcome of the game was a tie.
words.ex_cn: 比赛的结果是平局。
words.en: The outcome of an activity, process, or situation is the situation that exists at the end of it.

words.ex: The children are vibrant and full of energy.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们充满活力。
words.en: If you describe something as vibrant, you mean that it is bright, lively, and full of energy.

words.tr: n. 事件；一集；一段经历；
words.ex: The accident was a sad episode in his life.
words.ex_cn: 那场事故是他生命中的一件悲伤的事。
words.en: An episode is a part of a story that is broadcast on television or radio as one of a series, or a single event or group of related events.

words.ex: The reception at the hotel was very friendly.
words.ex_cn: 酒店的接待非常友好。
words.en: The act of receiving or being received, especially in a formal or official context.

words.tr:
v. 符合；合身；
adj. 健康的；适合的；
words.ex: This shirt fits me well.
words.ex_cn: 这件衬衫很合我的身。
words.en: If something fits, it is the right size and shape to go onto a person's body or onto a particular object.

words.ex: The river overflowed and broke the embankment.
words.ex_cn: 河水泛滥，冲垮了堤坝。
words.en: An embankment is a thick wall of earth that is built to carry a road or railway over an area of low ground, or to prevent water from a river or the sea from flooding an area.

words.tr:
v. 怒吼；吼叫；咆哮
n. 咆哮；怒号
words.ex: The bull bellowed loudly in the field.
words.ex_cn: 公牛在田野里大声吼叫。
words.en: If someone bellows, they shout angrily in a loud, deep voice.

words.ex: He tried to persuade her to stay.
words.ex_cn: 他试图说服她留下。
words.en: If you persuade someone to do something, you cause them to do it by giving them good reasons for doing it.

words.tr: n. 切片；薄片；部分；片段；
words.ex: She ate a slice of bread for breakfast.
words.ex_cn: 她早餐吃了一片面包。
words.en: A slice of something is a thin piece or portion of it.

words.ex: A megacity has more than ten million people.
words.ex_cn: 一个大城市有超过一千万人。
words.en: A megacity is a very large city, typically one with a population of over ten million people.

words.ex: The bird has a soft feather.
words.ex_cn: 这只鸟有一根柔软的羽毛。
words.en: One of the light, horny structures that form the principal covering of birds.

words.ex: The doctor gave him an antidote for the poison.
words.ex_cn: 医生给了他一种解毒剂来对抗毒药。
words.en: An antidote is a substance that counteracts the effects of poison or something harmful.

words.tr: v. 运转；操作；施行手术；
words.ex: The machine operates smoothly.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器运转顺畅。
words.en: If you operate a business or organization, you work to keep it running properly. If a business or organization operates, it carries out its work.

words.tr: v. 处理不当；使用不当
words.ex: He mishandled the situation and made it worse.
words.ex_cn: 他处理不当，让情况变得更糟。
words.en: If you mishandle something, you deal with it badly or carelessly, often causing problems or damage.

words.ex: Water can penetrate the soil slowly.
words.ex_cn: 水可以慢慢渗透进土壤。
words.en: To penetrate means to enter or pass through something, especially when this is difficult or when it is not obvious how to do it.

words.ex: He changed his job because of his background.
words.ex_cn: 他因为自己的背景换了工作。
words.en: The background is the situation that exists at a particular time, or the situation in which something happens, which helps to explain it.

words.ex: He is an architect who designs houses.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位设计房屋的建筑师。
words.en: An architect is a person who designs buildings and advises in their construction.

words.tr: n. 外观；外表；出现；露面；
words.ex: The appearance of the house surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这所房子的外观让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: The way that someone or something looks or the act of coming into view.

words.tr: v. 使年轻； 使恢复精神； 使复原
words.ex: The new sleep routine helps rejuvenate her energy.
words.ex_cn: 新的睡眠习惯帮助她恢复精力。
words.en: To rejuvenate someone or something means to make them look or feel young, fresh, or lively again.

words.tr: adj. 卓越的；杰出的；出类拔萃的
words.ex: He is a preeminent scientist in his field.
words.ex_cn: 他是该领域最杰出的科学家。
words.en: Standing out in importance or reputation; superior to all others.

words.ex: His nationality is Canadian.
words.ex_cn: 他的国籍是加拿大人。
words.en: Nationality is the legal relationship between an individual and a state, often used to refer to the country to which a person belongs.

words.tr:
v. 戳；刺；激励；督促
n. 戳；刺；催促
words.ex: He prodded the fire with a stick.
words.ex_cn: 他用一根棍子戳了戳火。
words.en: To poke or jab someone or something, often with a finger or a pointed object, in order to get their attention or to encourage them to do something.

words.tr: adj. 无数的；多的；数不清的；
words.ex: There are countless stars in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 夜空中有无数颗星星。
words.en: Too numerous to count.

words.ex: The pendulum oscillate slowly.
words.ex_cn: 钟摆缓慢地摆动。
words.en: If an object oscillates, it moves repeatedly from one position to another and back again, or if a figure or value oscillates, it keeps moving up and down.

words.tr: adj. 诚实的；说实话的；准确的
words.ex: He is a veracious person who always tells the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个诚实的人，总是说真话。
words.en: Someone who is veracious is truthful and honest.

words.ex: He is capable of solving hard math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他能解决复杂的数学问题。
words.en: If a person or thing is capable of doing something, they have the ability or potential to do it.

words.ex: He will enumerate the steps clearly.
words.ex_cn: 他将清晰地列出这些步骤。
words.en: To enumerate means to mention things one by one.

words.tr: adj. 有冒险精神的；敢于创新的；
words.ex: He is an adventurous boy who loves climbing mountains.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个喜欢爬山的有冒险精神的男孩。
words.en: Willing to take risks or to try out new methods, ideas, or experiences.

words.ex: This phone is superior to the old one.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机比旧的更好。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as superior, you mean that they are better than other people or things.

words.tr:
n. 滥用；虐待；辱骂；
v. 滥用；虐待；辱骂；
words.ex: The abuse of power led to many problems.
words.ex_cn: 权力的滥用导致了许多问题。
words.en: Abuse is the improper usage or treatment of a thing, often to unfairly or improperly gain benefit. Abuse can come in many forms, such as physical or verbal maltreatment, injury, assault, violation, rape, unjust practices, crimes, or other types of aggression.

words.tr:
n. 鱼饵；诱惑物
v. 下诱饵
words.ex: He used bread as bait to catch fish.
words.ex_cn: 他用面包当诱饵来钓鱼。
words.en: Bait is something which is used to attract fish or animals so that they can be caught. It can also refer to something that is offered to someone to persuade them to do something.

words.ex: She is pregnant and will have a baby next month.
words.ex_cn: 她怀孕了，下个月就要生宝宝了。
words.en: Having a baby developing in the uterus.

words.ex: The doctor used drops to dilate her pupils.
words.ex_cn: 医生用了滴眼液来扩大她的瞳孔。
words.en: If you dilate something such as a part of your body, or if it dilates, it becomes larger or wider.

words.tr:
v. 挣扎；深陷困境
n. 比目鱼
words.ex: The fish floundered in the shallow water.
words.ex_cn: 鱼在浅水中挣扎。
words.en: If you flounder, you experience great difficulties and are likely to fail completely.

words.ex: They conspire to cheat on the test.
words.ex_cn: 他们密谋在考试中作弊。
words.en: If two or more people or groups conspire to do something illegal or harmful, they make a secret agreement to do it.

words.ex: The keystone holds the arch together.
words.ex_cn: 拱顶石将拱门固定在一起。
words.en: A keystone is the central, topmost stone in an arch, which holds all the other stones in place. Metaphorically, it refers to the central principle or part of a system, plan, etc., upon which all else depends.

words.tr: adj. 公开的；明显的；公然的
words.ex: His anger was overt and hard to miss.
words.ex_cn: 他的愤怒是明显的，很难忽视。
words.en: An overt action or attitude is done or shown in an open and obvious way.

words.ex: The company paid indemnity for the damaged car.
words.ex_cn: 公司为损坏的汽车支付了保险赔偿。
words.en: If something provides indemnity, it provides insurance or protection against damage or loss, especially in the form of a legal agreement.

words.tr: v. 反复地说；重申；重述
words.ex: He reiterate that he is sorry.
words.ex_cn: 他反复地说他很抱歉。
words.en: If you reiterate something, you say it again, usually in order to emphasize it.

words.ex: The student was insubordinate to the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 这名学生对老师不服从。
words.en: If someone is insubordinate, they deliberately do not obey someone of higher rank.

words.tr:
v. 逝去；过去
n. （光阴）逝去
words.ex: Two hours elapsed while he waited for the bus.
words.ex_cn: 他等公交车时，两个小时过去了。
words.en: If time elapses, it passes.

words.ex: The barbaric act shocked everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这个野蛮的行为震惊了所有人。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as barbaric, you mean that it is extremely cruel or uncivilized.

words.tr: adj. 值得拥有的；令人渴望的；称心如意的；
words.ex: A quiet neighborhood is desirable for families.
words.ex_cn: 安静的社区对家庭来说是值得拥有的。
words.en: Something that is desirable is worth having or doing because it is useful, necessary, or popular.

words.ex: The boy disobeyed his mother.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩违抗了他妈妈。
words.en: If you disobey someone or something, you deliberately do not do what they say or what they tell you to do.

words.tr: n. 理事会；委员会；议会；
words.ex: The city council made a new rule about recycling.
words.ex_cn: 市政府理事会制定了关于回收的新规定。
words.en: A council is a group of people who are elected to govern a local area such as a city or, in Britain, a county.

words.ex: There are innumerable stars in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 夜空中有数不清的星星。
words.en: Too many to be counted; very many.

words.ex: The roses are in bloom in spring.
words.ex_cn: 玫瑰在春天开花。
words.en: When a plant or tree blooms, it produces flowers. The period during which a plant or tree produces flowers is also known as its bloom.

words.ex: The boss can override the rules if needed.
words.ex_cn: 如果需要，老板可以凌驾于规则之上。
words.en: If one thing in a situation overrides other things, it is more important than them.

words.ex: The universe may be infinite.
words.ex_cn: 宇宙可能是无限的。
words.en: If you describe something as infinite, you are emphasizing that it is extremely great in amount or degree.

words.tr:
n. 锻造车间；
v. 建立（联系等）；
words.ex: The blacksmith works in the forge every morning.
words.ex_cn: 铁匠每天早上都在锻造车间工作。
words.en: To forge something means to create it, especially by using considerable effort or skill. It can also mean to make or produce something, especially with some difficulty or effort. Additionally, it refers to the act of making a copy or imitation of something with the intent to deceive.

words.tr:
adv. 在夜里；突然；
adj. 整晚的；
words.ex: The baby slept overnight in the crib.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿整夜睡在小床上。
words.en: If something happens overnight, it happens during the night or for the period of one night. It can also mean happening very quickly or suddenly.

words.tr: v. 焚化；焚毁；把…烧成灰烬
words.ex: The city will incinerate the trash tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市明天将焚烧垃圾。
words.en: To incinerate something means to burn it until it is reduced to ash.

words.tr:
v. 交配繁殖；饲养；
n. 品种；
words.ex: The farmers breed cows to get more milk.
words.ex_cn: 农民让奶牛交配繁殖以获得更多牛奶。
words.en: If you breed animals or plants, you keep them for the purpose of producing more animals or plants with particular qualities, in a controlled way.

words.tr:
n. 薄片；小片
v. 使成薄片；（成小薄片）脱落
words.ex: A flake fell from the ceiling.
words.ex_cn: 一片碎屑从天花板上掉了下来。
words.en: A flake is a small, thin piece of something that has broken off from a larger piece, or a person who is considered unreliable or eccentric.

words.tr:
adj. 最重要的；
adv. 首要地；
words.ex: He is the foremost expert in this field.
words.ex_cn: 他是这个领域最重要的专家。
words.en: Most important or prominent; leading.

words.ex: He looked at the lie with contempt.
words.ex_cn: 他轻蔑地看着这个谎言。
words.en: If you have contempt for someone or something, you have no respect for them or think that they are unimportant.

words.tr: adj. 耻辱的；不名誉的；不光彩的
words.ex: He faced an ignominious defeat in the election.
words.ex_cn: 他在选举中遭遇了耻辱的失败。
words.en: If you describe an experience or action as ignominious, you mean it is embarrassing because it shows a great lack of success.

words.tr: v. 使客观化；使具体化；物化
words.ex: He tries to objectify his feelings to understand them better.
words.ex_cn: 他试图使自己的感受客观化，以便更好地理解它们。
words.en: To represent something abstract as a concrete object; to treat someone as a mere object.

words.tr:
v. 获得；增加；
n. 增益；获得；
words.ex: He gained a new skill last month.
words.ex_cn: 他上个月获得了一项新技能。
words.en: To gain means to obtain something that is useful, that gives you an advantage, or that is in some way positive, especially over a period of time.

words.tr:
v. 缩进排版；使呈锯齿状
n. 订货单
words.ex: Please indent the first line of each paragraph.
words.ex_cn: 请将每段的第一行缩进。
words.en: To start a line of text further from the margin than the main part of the text.

words.ex: The rain persisted all day.
words.ex_cn: 雨持续了一整天。
words.en: If you persist in doing something, you continue to do it even though it is difficult or other people are against it.

words.ex: He visits his grandparents every fortnight.
words.ex_cn: 他每两周拜访一次祖父母。
words.en: A fortnight is a period of two weeks.

words.ex: He bought a repair kit for his bike.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一套自行车维修工具。
words.en: A kit is a group of items that are kept together, often in the same container, because they are all used for similar purposes.

words.ex: He never disparages his classmates.
words.ex_cn: 他从不贬低他的同学。
words.en: If you disparage someone or something, you speak about them in a way which shows that you do not have a good opinion of them.

words.ex: You need to pay a 40-yuan deposit to rent the bike.
words.ex_cn: 租自行车需要支付40元押金。
